title: General-lfp integral complexes have sequential internal-Hom continuity
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $X$ a locally Noetherian, quasi-compact scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B=p_X^*\underline R$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $H_B=R\mathcal Hom_B$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $K\in D(B)$ have bounded general-ring-object constructible cohomology [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: each cohomology sheaf admits a finite constructible locally closed stratification on whose strata it is pro-étale locally a cokernel $B^m\to B^n$ with finite $m,n$ and arbitrary section-valued entries.

The underlying topological space of $X$ satisfies the descending chain condition on closed subsets. Each cohomology sheaf of $K$ admits a finite constructible stratification with pro-étale local models $B_V\otimes_R P$, where $P$ is a finitely presented scalar $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; torsion $P$ and degree-dependent stratifications are allowed. The category of $B$-module sheaves has exact small filtered colimits. For every sequential diagram $(M_n^\bullet)$ of $B$-module complexes with a common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced map
$$\varinjlim_n H_B(K,M_n^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_B(K,\varinjlim_n M_n^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(B)$, independent of representatives. Colimits are exact termwise sheaf-module colimits, on the left using functorial internal-Hom representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No constructibility or completeness of $M_n$ is required.

For any complex $C$ representing $L\in D(B)$ and any $c\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^q(L)=0$ for $q<c$, the complex $P$ defined by $P^q=0$ for $q<c$, $P^c=\operatorname{coker}(d_C^{c-1})$, and $P^q=C^q$ for $q>c$, with induced differentials, receives a scalar-equivariant quasi-isomorphism $C\to P$. Consequently the repeated-$\ell$ tower on $P$ is a representative of the scalar tower on $L$ to which the displayed continuity isomorphism applies. No assumption beyond the cohomological lower bound is imposed on $L$.

proof.text: A quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme is Noetherian. The existing Mathlib scheme instance gives NoetherianSpace X, which includes the descending-chain condition on closed subsets recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal].

source.place: Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology; descending-chain consequence of minimality

proof.text: For each degree $q$ with nonzero $H^q(K)$, apply implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] to $M=H^q(K)$, $A=R$, and this Noetherian $X$. Its hypothesis (i) is exactly the assumed finite stratification with arbitrary section-valued finite presentation matrices. Its conclusion gives a finite constructible stratification and pro-étale local models $B_V\otimes_R P$ for finitely presented scalar $R$-modules $P$. It allows torsion and does not require the old and new stratifications to coincide. Apply it separately in each of the finitely many relevant degrees; boundedness of the cohomology is unchanged. Hence $K$ has bounded cohomology constructible in the finite constant local model sense.

proof.text: Use the existing Grothendieck-abelian instance for internal module objects over the pulled-back commutative condensed ring. Its general categorical consequences give colimits and AB5 in the site universe; universe shrinking gives exact sequential colimits. Construct a functorial representative of derived Hom by functorial K-injective resolution followed by the ordinary Hom complex out of a homotopy representative of K. The right-derived-functor unit is invertible on K-injectives, and the resolution augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Their natural isomorphisms identify this model after localization with the existing derived internal Hom.

First identify the two existing models of the integral coefficient ring explicitly: the valuation subring of WithAbs E and the valuation subring of E with its transferred norm are isometrically ring-isomorphic, by the identity on underlying elements. Postcomposition on continuous maps produces an isomorphism of condensed rings. Restriction of scalars along its inverse is an exact monoidal equivalence, and preserves finite constant constructibility by the transport argument of [lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible]. Tensor/Hom adjunctions identify the derived Hom functors under this equivalence. Use the cohomologically bounded diagram-continuity property proved inside [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity]: its closed-model, open-extension and triangulated generation steps give this stronger property before the final conversion from termwise bounds. Transport it through the coefficient equivalence. Lift the index category of natural numbers to the site universe and transfer the colimit cocone across that equivalence. For a termwise bounded-below diagram, the localized complexes have the same cohomological lower bound. Exact sequential colimits commute with cohomology; naturality of any representative identification e then shows that the canonical comparison is an isomorphism. Exact sequential colimits also preserve objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. For M to N, naturality of colimit.post transfers the colimit-cocone property to N even without a termwise bound on N. Compose the comparison for M, derived Hom of the localized colimit map, and the inverse comparison for N. Cancellation of the latter proves uniqueness of the required isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), internal-Hom filtered continuity; compare Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.12 (global direct sums only)

proof.text: For the final assertion construct $P$ with the terms in the statement. Since $d_C^c d_C^{c-1}=0$, $d_C^c$ factors through $C^c/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{c-1})$ and defines $d_P^c$; its composite with $d_C^{c+1}$ is zero. Let $u:C\to P$ be zero below $c$, the quotient map at $c$, and the identity above $c$. These formulas commute with differentials. At degree $c$ one has $\ker(d_P^c)=\ker(d_C^c)/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{c-1})$ and no incoming image, so $H^c(u)$ is an isomorphism. At degree $c+1$, the image of $d_P^c$ is the image of $d_C^c$ because the quotient map is epic; in every higher degree the cohomology calculation is unchanged. Below $c$ both cohomologies vanish by hypothesis. Thus $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], including when $C$ itself is unbounded below.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical quotient truncation (with cohomological indexing)

proof.text: Every map in the construction of $u$ is $B$-linear, so $u\circ\ell=\ell\circ u$ in every degree: at $c$ this is $[\ell x]=\ell[x]$, and elsewhere it is immediate for zero or identity maps. Consequently the maps $u$ at all stages give a morphism from the repeated-$\ell$ sequence of $C$ to that of $P$, each component a quasi-isomorphism. Under the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the latter sequence represents the scalar sequence of $L$. It has the common termwise lower bound $c$, so [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity], specialized exactly as in step 4, applies. Its representative-independence identifies the comparison with the one for the scalar sequence of $L$. This uses only the cohomological lower bound on $L$.
